messages:
maya: FYI support escalated a customer (acct: acme-504) — p99 latency jumped from ~180ms -> ~1.2s last 3 hours, intermittent OOMs on /v1/chat/completions. They attached logs and repro steps.
henry: linking their logs here. looks like GPU memory reserved keeps growing even when active alloc drops. suspect KV cache growth + fragmentation. nvidia-smi shows memory used oscillating but reserved stays high.
maya: customer timeline — long-running chat sessions with many back-and-forth messages (avg session tokens ~25k). They say issue started after our model rollout 2026-03-10 (quantized variant).
julia: quick numbers from our telemetry: p95 up 2.8x, p99 up ~6.5x for that tenant in 3h window. error rate (503 OOM) at 0.6% of requests for that pool.
kevin: copied some of the node metrics: 
```
# from node gpu host (sample)
Timestamp: 2026-03-14T18:02:01Z
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
12032 MiB, 49152 MiB
# process-level: python allocator reports
torch.cuda.memory_allocated(): 11.6 GiB
torch.cuda.memory_reserved(): 28.9 GiB
# fragmentation estimate: reserved - allocated ~17.3 GiB
```
henry: that delta is the crux — fragmentation / caching keeps large reserved blocks so batching sometimes can't allocate for new KV buffers => requests slow while runtime attempts to fallback or triggers GC.
maya: did we see similar pattern in previous regression (1830200000-gpu-oom-frag-kv-regression)? how is this different?
henry: similar root cause but slightly different trigger. earlier incident was a model change that changed tensor lifetimes; this one looks like sustained KV growth from long sessions + heavier quantized kernels that allocate more reserved memory. Also observed repeated `cudaMalloc` retries in logs.
julia: I captured a sample request trace (trimmed):
```
Request start 18:00:00
routing -> model-worker-34
batching wait 120ms
kv-mgr: ensure_space for 18MB -> failed, trying GC
allocator: cudaMalloc failed, sleeping 50ms, retry
attempt fallback to smaller batch -> took 400ms
response returned 18:00:01.18 (+1.18s)
```
kevin: customer repro script (they gave) — heavy chat app that appends past turns to context for every message. I'll paste simplified version:
```
# pseudo repro (python)
for i in range(10000):
  messages.append(user_msg)
  res = requests.post(api, json={"model":"rwood-quant-v2","messages":messages})
```
This increments KV each loop.
maya: immediate impact mitigation suggestions? we need to reduce p99 ASAP for customer.
henry: short-term (minutes): 1) throttle that customer's concurrency and/or apply per-session token cap (support can implement rule) 2) fallback route to older non-quantized model variant (less kv per token) 3) schedule rolling restart of affected workers in that pool to release reserved caches (cheap but disruptive).
julia: operational steps I did: rolled a canary restart on one worker -> memory_reserved dropped from ~29GiB -> 9GiB and p99 on that worker recovered. Confirmed restarts reclaim reserved even though fragmentation persists in general.
kevin: rolling restart is fastest, but not ideal at scale. For a 100-worker pool doing cold restarts will increase latency for the rest. Recommend targeted restarts for customer's sharded nodes.
henry: medium-term (days): implement per-session KV caps + eviction (LRU drop older turns beyond N tokens); enforce max_memory_per_session at the runtime level so a single noisy session can't starve pool.
julia: long-term (weeks): allocator/engine changes: 1) tune TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF (e.g., max_split_size_mb, garbage_collection_threshold) to reduce large-fragment allocations; 2) test enabling `max_split_size_mb:32` vs current 512 to encourage splitting; 3) evaluate a periodic lightweight model worker process that compacts/restarts only when fragmentation crosses threshold (>30% reserved gap).
kevin: propose a short-term config toggle we can flip per-pool: `runtime.max_session_kv_tokens` and `runtime.enforce_compact_restarts` to schedule restarts during low traffic windows.
henry: also logging improvement: add `cuda_mem_summary` sample to traces when batch fails (so we can attribute which request caused fragmentation). add metric `gpu_reserved_minus_allocated` per-worker and alert when > 10GB sustained.
maya: can we push emergency changelist (hotfix) to enforce per-session cap as config in gateway? timeline?
ulia: (typo?) — julia: I can shepherd a small gateway guard that rejects requests exceeding a session token threshold (configurable) — 2-3 hours to get through canary + deploy.
henry: I'll draft runtime patch for an LRU drop-on-append inside KV manager (workload safe) — probably needs a bit more testing (~3 days). This prevents unbounded KV growth.
kevin: also check quantization variant — maybe our quantized kernels allocate aligned buffers slightly differently causing fragmentation. Recommend perf/quant team run microbench kernels to confirm. cc @sre-oncall for infra-level mitigations.
sre-oncall: oncall visibility — we can schedule targeted restarts and set node-level OOM-killer tolerances if needed. Also can temporarily raise the pool capacity (spin up extra nodes) to absorb until proper fix is in.
julia: reproduction steps for ENG to reproduce locally: 1) run a model-worker with same quantized artifact 2) run load script simulating many append-to-context chat sessions (attached below) 3) monitor `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()` vs `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` and `nvidia-smi -l 1`
```
# load script sketch (wrk-like)
CONC=8
for c in $(seq 1 $CONC); do
  python chat_flood.py --session_length 25000 --requests 5000 &
done
# monitor
watch -n1 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv"
```
henry: local repro confirmed where reserved climbs ~3x allocated after 30 minutes of that pattern. I also saw `cublas` workspace spikes.
kevin: diagnostic checklist I've run/ask for: 
- kernel: cuda/driver versions (did rollout change driver?)
- torch/trimmed runtime build flags
- quant kernels changed alignment allocations?
- batch sizes distribution; any sudden increases in batch size -> causes big mallocs
- KV per-session growth histograms (we need to emit)
Please paste answers in thread.
maya: Support action: I'll ask customer to throttle for now and give ETA for gateway cap deploy. Also offer them temporary dedicated pool (paid) as fallback.
julia: I pushed a canary gateway guard to staging (rejects sessions > 30k tokens) and started a canary restart on a customer worker. Observing p99 drop on canary immediately.
henry: follow-ups assigned:
- henry: runtime LRU cap PR (3d)
- julia: gateway guard + prod roll (2-4h)
- kevin: quant perf microbench + driver check (1d)
- sre-oncall: orchestrate targeted restarts + temporary capacity (now)
- maya: coordinate with customer + support comms (now)

maya: thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary to the customer and reopen thread if anything new shows up. :thumbsup:
